stories.title: 'Locked into the moment,' Bryce Young rallies first-place Panthers past Ravens
stories.summary: In a back-and-forth game laced with lead changes, Bryce Young rallied the Panthers to a 35-33 home win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday at Bank of America Stadium, a second straight victory for the 5-5 Panthers that padded lead in the NFC South.
stories.detail: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- With the game on the line, Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales wants quarterback Bryce Young in the driver's seat. And the fourth-year QB -- whom Canales benched in 2024 -- showed exactly why he's earned that trust from his boss in a 35-33 come-from-behind home win over the Baltimore Ravens (4-7) on Sunday at Bank of America Stadium. Young drove the Panthers' offense 55 yards down the field to set up a game-winning 37-yard field goal for kicker Ryan Fitzgerald with 1:44 left in the fourth quarter. After the ball flew through the uprights, Young ultimately produced the 14th game-winning drive of his career and the fifth win of Carolina's up-and-down season. "Game on the line, there's nobody else I want with the ball," Canales said. "Bryce Young is going to go there, he's going to be in control, he's going to be focused and locked into the moment, and that's what he looked like on that drive." Canales and Young have come a long way since 2024 when the then-second-year QB was shelved for backup Andy Dalton ahead of the coach's third-ever regular-season game. Young returned to the lineup after being benched for five games, and he hasn't really looked back since. La…

stories.title: Tyler Shough voices confidence in Saints, Kellen Moore after 3-7 start
stories.summary: Two straight losses. Justin Reid being released. Run game a mess. Despite the challenges, there's belief New Orleans can turn things around.
stories.detail: CHICAGO -- It has been a month of turmoil for the New Orleans Saints and quarterback Tyler Shough . The Saints fell to 3-7 on Sunday after a 21-13 loss to the Chicago Bears , a loss that effectively seals their postseason fate unless they find a way to run the table in their final seven games. With the Cincinnati Bengals and their top-ranked passing offense up next in Week 12, that will be a tall task. Beyond Sunday's loss, team captain Justin Reid asked for, and was granted his release just last week. There have been injuries to the offensive line and kicking issues have persisted despite a change this month. The Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti , but the starting quarterback remains the team's leading rusher. Despite the seven losses, Shough said he still believes New Orleans is a good team. The QB noted the Saints have been in every game except the Week 4 loss to the Atlanta Falcons . Right now, Shough says it's "a great opportunity for myself and everybody to look in the mirror and understand how bad [they] really want this." He admitted it's not going to be easy. stories.title: Bills' Grand Theft Auto VI-themed jab at Dolphins tops NFL Week 11 trolls
stories.summary: NFL teams remained petty in Week 11, led by a petty post from the Buffalo Bills.
stories.detail: Grand Theft Auto VI has taken over the entertainment world since its release last Thursday. The video game's reach carried over to the NFL, too, becoming the theme of a petty post on Sunday. The Buffalo Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins 26-9 led by its defense. Buffalo allowed just 185 yards and picked off Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord once. Josh Allen had two interceptions himself, but he also threw for 304 yards and a score. Other teams such as the New York Jets and Chicago Bears tapped into the GTA VI space, but the Bills' attempt felt more direct as they faced the Dolphins. The victory prompted Buffalo to post a custom game cover inspired by that of GTA VI, which is set in "Vice City," a fictional version of Miami. Instead of it reading "GTA VI" across the cover, the Bills added: "Bills Win" with players scattered throughout it. Here are the top trolls from NFL's Week 11. I'm not sure it would have been an overreaction by me, and I'm not sure it was an overreaction by the Colts. We are entering the fish-or-cut-bait time of the year in the NFL. Thanksgiving is in four days. December starts next week. At this point, if something isn't working, we're past the time for patience. If you're still in the race, every move you make must be about what could make the difference in your favor. If you're out of it, every move needs to be about figuring out the plan for 2027 and beyond. The Colts concluded that they weren't going anywhere with Jones and it was time to get another look at Anthony Richardson Sr . teamStories.title: Jonah Coleman powers Broncos past Raiders 38-24 as Denver honors the late Tom Jackson
teamStories.summary: — Rookie Jonah Coleman ran for a season-best 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on a solemn Sunday in the Mile High City as they honored “Orange Crush” and ESPN great
teamStories.detail: DENVER -- — Rookie Jonah Coleman ran for a season-best 111 yards and three touchdowns and the Denver Broncos beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 on a solemn Sunday in the Mile High City as they honored “Orange Crush” and ESPN great Tom Jackson following his death at age 75. Jackson's death was announced by longtime on-air partner Chris Berman just as some of the Broncos' early risers were starting to arrive at Empower Field for top overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza 's first career road start. For the coin flip, Broncos great Champ Bailey wore a No. 57 Jackson jersey following a moment of silence and a video tribute to the fiery cornerstone of the defense that led Denver to its first Super Bowl appearance in 1977. Ja'Quan McMillian sealed the victory with a 35-yard, one-handed pick-6 with 1:52 remaining and the Broncos (8-2) clinging to a seven-point lead. Coleman scored on runs of 1, 4 and 7 yards, the latter two after the Raiders (4-7) had erased a 17-0 deficit. The Broncos kept pace with Kansas City atop the AFC West by winning their sixth consecutive game since coach Sean Payton took back the offensive play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb . stories.title: Klay Thompson blows out shoe as Heat take on Thunder
stories.summary: Klay Thompson blew out part of a shoe while defending a fast break in the Heat's game against the Thunder on Sunday night.
stories.detail: MIAMI -- Klay Thompson blew out part of a shoe while defending a fast break in the Miami Heat 's game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday night. Thompson was defending a drive by Thunder guard Ajay Mitchell when it appeared a part of his shoe -- possibly an insert -- somehow detached itself with about 5 minutes left in the opening quarter. Mitchell scored, and play was stopped moments later when referees noticed that part of the shoe was around midcourt. Miami called timeout, and Thompson was lacing up his right shoe on the bench moments later. Thompson returned to the game midway through the second quarter. He is fourth on the NBA's all-time 3-pointers made list, on pace to catch former Heat guard Ray Allen for the No. 3 spot by the end of November.

stories.title: Bulls G Norman Powell sidelined by mild hamstring injury
stories.summary: Bulls guard Norman Powell was ruled out against the Nuggets and will be reevaluated later in the week because of a mild right hamstring strain.
stories.detail: CHICAGO -- Bulls guard Norman Powell was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nuggets because of a mild right hamstring strain. Powell got hurt during Friday night's 98-94 loss to the Washington Wizards . The team said Powell will be evaluated later this week. "It was bothering him but we didn't know at what point was it," Bulls coach Tiago Splitter said before Sunday's game, adding that an MRI indicated the strain was mild. The 33-year-old Powell is averaging a team-high 20.8 points per game in his first season with Chicago. He scored 16 points against the Wizards on 7-for-18 shooting. Powell signed a two-year deal with the Bulls in free agency that could be worth up to $45 million. The veteran guard played for the Miami Heat last season, averaging 21.7 points in 58 games while earning an All-Star selection for the first time. "Norm's been great, helping teammates, even the coaching staff," Splitter said. "His knowledge of the game, his experience being in the NBA Finals, it's always valuable. It adds value having a guy like that in the locker room, around the players. We're going to miss him on the court but he's going to keep helping us in the locker room." Chicago rookie Ca…

teamStories.detail: Today I’m going to do something I don’t usually do here. I’m going to complain. And it’s a crazy feeling, complaining about a win like last night’s. It just doesn’t sit right. And, in a way, it feels oddly ungrateful. Hypocritical, even. Especially when you’ve spent a not-insignificant amount of time advocating for people to just chill out a little bit and enjoy the ride. Look, last night was great. The Spurs took over the lead for the last time at the end of the 1st quarter, and it never really felt like they were challenged after that. The Pelicans got within six points of them with about four minutes left in the 2nd half, and then Wemby slammed the door on them so hard that you could almost hear metaphorical hinges rattle. The Spurs were up by thirteen in roughly a minute-and-a-half, and that was that. They spent most of the 2nd half up by 20+ plus points, and Wemby sat with six minutes left in the fourth, after absolutely drilling a pair of threes to crush what little spirit the Pelicans had remaining, and get to that nice round number of fifty points. And all I could think was: “What the hell am I supposed to write about this?” I know. Victor Wembanyama dropped his 2nd Wilt C…
